title: 2020 HMMT February Team Problem 7
statement:
Positive real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy

\[||\cdots|||x|-y|-x| \cdots-y|-x|=||\cdots|||y|-x|-y| \cdots-x|-y|\]

where there are 2019 absolute value signs \(|\cdot|\) on each side. Determine, with proof, all possible values of \(\frac{x}{y}\).

solutions.text:
Clearly \(x=y\) works. Else WLOG \(x<y\), define \(d=y-x\), and define \(f(z):=||z-y|-x|\) so our expression reduces to

\[f^{1009}(x)=\left|f^{1009}(0)-y\right|\]

Now note that for \(z \in[0, y], f(z)\) can be written as

\[f(z)= \begin{cases}d-z, & 0 \leq z \leq d \\ z-d, & d<z \leq y\end{cases}\]

Hence \(f(f(z))=f(d-z)=z\) for all \(z \in[0, d]\). Therefore

\[\left|f^{1009}(0)-y\right|=|f(0)-y|=x\]

If \(x>d\) then \(f^{1009}(x)<x\) which is impossible (if \(f^{1009}(x) \leq d\) then the conclusion trivially holds, and if \(f^{1009}(x)>d\) we must have \(\left.f^{1009}(x)=x-1009 d<x\right)\). Therefore \(x \leq d\), so \(f^{1009}(x)=f(x)=d-x\) and we must have \(d-x=x\). Hence \(y=3 x\) which is easily seen to work. To summarize, the possible values of \(\frac{x}{y}\) are \(\frac{1}{3}, 1,3\).
